Police and military suppression measures had limited effect, with prisons overcrowded and gangs continuing to operate from inside. Gang violence became main cause of new migration wave, with tens of thousands of Salvadorans fleeing to United States seeking asylum. Problem roots included poverty, inequality, lack of opportunity, and violent culture left from civil war.

events.title: Dollarization Formally Implemented
events.description: El Salvador formally adopted U.S. dollar as legal tender, replacing colón. Dollarization policy was promoted by ARENA government, aiming to stabilize economy, lower interest rates, and attract foreign investment. Supporters believed dollarization would eliminate currency risk, promoting trade and remittance flows with United States. Critics warned El Salvador would lose monetary policy independence, unable to respond to economic shocks through devaluation. Dollarization tightly bound Salvadoran economy to U.S. economy, dependent on remittances from United States (about 20% of GDP). Inflation initially rose, with merchants taking opportunity to raise prices. Dollarization was considered favorable to business elites and large corporations, but impact on ordinary people was complex. Policy was highly controversial, reflecting right-wing free market orientation of Salvadoran economic policy. Dollarization was extreme measure taken by few Latin American countries, reflecting distrust of national currency.

events.title: CAFTA Free Trade Agreement
events.description: El Salvador signed and ratified Central America Free Trade Agreement (CAFTA), establishing free trade zone with United States and other Central American countries. Agreement eliminated tariffs, opened markets, protected intellectual property and investment. ARENA government enthusiastically supported it, claiming it would promote exports, create jobs, and attract investment. Opposition included FMLN, peasant organizations, and unions, fearing agreement would destroy small farmer economy, letting U.S. large corporations dominate market. Agreement caused intense debate in congress, ultimately passing by narrow majority. CAFTA deepened El Salvador's economic integration with United States, with textile and agricultural exports increasing. However, small farmers faced competition from cheap U.S. agricultural products (like corn and rice), with many going bankrupt. Agreement reflected neoliberal economic policy dominance, but social impact was polarized.

events.title: FMLN First Electoral Victory
events.description: FMLN candidate Mauricio Funes defeated ARENA in presidential election, achieving historic victory and ending ARENA's 20-year consecutive rule. Funes was moderate television journalist; though representing FMLN, not former guerrilla, helping attract centrist voters. Victory reflected popular disappointment with ARENA, including high crime rates, economic inequality, and corruption. Funes promised social reforms but also guaranteed no radical changes, maintaining relations with United States and free market policies. FMLN victory marked major shift in Salvadoran politics, with former revolutionary guerrillas legitimately gaining power through ballot. However, Funes government was constrained by FMLN internal hardliners, also facing opposition resistance and business pressure. During tenure, Funes attempted to balance social policies and business interests, implementing some anti-poverty programs, but economic problems and violent crime continued to plague.

events.title: Gang Truce Agreement
events.description: With government support, MS-13 and 18th Street Gang reached historic truce agreement, promising to stop mutual killings. Agreement was brokered by Catholic Church and former guerrilla mediators, with government transferring gang leaders from maximum security prisons to better conditions as return. Truce initially showed significant effect, with murder rate dropping over 50%, from 14 daily to 5. International community praised as innovative crime control strategy. However, truce was highly controversial, with critics accusing government of negotiating with criminal organizations, questioning its legitimacy and sustainability. Truce details were secretive, lacking transparency. Two years later, truce gradually collapsed, with gangs resuming violence and murder rate soaring again. Truce failure reasons included lack of economic and social integration programs, gang internal divisions, and political exploitation. Experience showed confronting gang violence required comprehensive strategy, not simple negotiation or suppression.

events.title: Salvador Sánchez Cerén Elected
events.description: FMLN candidate Salvador Sánchez Cerén narrowly defeated ARENA candidate Norman Quijano in presidential election. Cerén was former guerrilla commander, representing FMLN hardliners. Victory showed FMLN consolidating governing position, but close election results reflected deep social divisions. Cerén government promised social programs, including education, healthcare, and pension reforms. However, during tenure faced severe challenges, including soaring gang violence, economic stagnation, and drought crisis. 2015-2016, El Salvador became country with world's highest murder rate, over 100 murders per 100,000 population. Government adopted tough security policies, including 'extraordinary measures,' allowing police and military greater power to combat gangs. However, human rights organizations criticized excessive use of force and extrajudicial executions. Cerén government also faced corruption allegations, undermining its legitimacy.

events.title: Violence Crisis Peak
events.description: El Salvador experienced most violent year on record, with over 6,600 murders, murder rate reaching 103 per 100,000, making it world's most dangerous non-war country. Gang violence spiraled out of control, with MS-13 and 18th Street Gang openly battling police and military. Gangs extorted buses, taxis, and businesses, with those refusing to pay being killed. Police and military adopted more aggressive strategies, with gang member encounters often ending in death. Human rights organizations documented hundreds of suspected police extrajudicial execution cases. Many arrested were not gang members, detained based on appearance or residence. Prisons overcrowded, difficult to control, with gangs continuing to command criminal activities from inside. Government implemented special security plans, mobilizing thousands of soldiers to patrol streets. Violence crisis triggered new migration wave, with tens of thousands, particularly youth and families, fleeing to seek asylum in United States. Crisis exposed state's inability to control gangs and deep social problems including poverty, inequality, and lack of opportunity.

events.title: Amnesty Law Abolished
events.description: El Salvador Supreme Court ruled 1993 amnesty law unconstitutional, opening door to prosecuting civil war crimes. Amnesty law had exempted almost all crimes from 1980-1992 civil war, preventing accountability for government forces and guerrillas' war crimes. Court ruling responded to decades of advocacy by human rights organizations and victims' families. Decision was praised by international community, viewed as victory for justice. However, actual prosecutions progressed slowly, with very few cases going to trial. In 2020, former Colonel Inocente Montano was convicted for participating in Jesuit priest murders, first high-ranking officer convicted for civil war crimes. Abolishing amnesty law symbolized El Salvador's move toward transitional justice, but true accountability still faced political, judicial, and social obstacles. Many involved had died, evidence lost, political will insufficient. Nation still struggled to face civil war legacy and achieve justice for victims.

events.title: Migrant Caravan
events.description: Thousands of Central American migrants, including many Salvadorans, formed 'caravan' collectively heading toward United States, attracting international attention. Migrants fled violence, poverty, and lack of opportunity, seeking better life and safety in United States. Caravan traveled through Mexico toward U.S.-Mexico border, receiving humanitarian aid along the way. U.S. Trump administration portrayed caravan as threat, sending troops to border and tightening asylum policies. Caravan highlighted humanitarian crisis in Central American Northern Triangle (El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras). Gang violence, government corruption, and climate change (causing drought and agricultural failure) forced hundreds of thousands to leave homes. El Salvador has estimated 2.5 million diaspora in United States, with remittances being nation's economic lifeline. Trump threatened to cut aid to El Salvador, forcing government to stop migrants. Crisis showed regional problems required comprehensive solutions, not just border enforcement.

events.title: Nayib Bukele Electoral Victory
events.description: Outsider candidate Nayib Bukele overwhelmingly defeated ARENA and FMLN in presidential election, ending two-party dominance of 30-year political landscape. Bukele was young entrepreneur and former San Salvador mayor, running as Nuevas Ideas (New Ideas) candidate. He attracted voters with anti-corruption, anti-establishment populist message, promising to eradicate gang violence and restore security. Bukele was skilled at social media, using Twitter and Facebook to communicate directly with people, shaping young, modern, decisive image. Victory reflected popular profound disappointment with traditional parties, considering both corrupt and incompetent, failing to solve violence and poverty problems. Bukele was elected at 37, El Salvador's youngest president in modern history. His rise marked part of Latin American populism and political fragmentation trend. Bukele's governing style would prove highly controversial, triggering debate about democracy and authoritarianism.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic Response
events.description: COVID-19 pandemic struck El Salvador, with Bukele government implementing one of Latin America's strictest lockdown measures. Government closed borders, schools, and businesses, implementing mandatory quarantine, with violators detained in 'quarantine centers.' Police and military strictly enforced lockdown, arresting thousands of violators. Measures initially effectively controlled virus spread but severely impacted economy, with hundreds of thousands unemployed and poverty rate rising. Government distributed food packages and cash aid, but corruption and unequal distribution drew criticism. Supreme Court ruled some lockdown measures unconstitutional, with Bukele publicly criticizing court. During pandemic, Bukele used emergency powers to consolidate control, weakening oversight institutions. Healthcare system strained, hospitals overloaded, healthcare workers lacking protective equipment. Vaccination began in 2021, with Bukele actively procuring vaccines, promoting as achievement. Pandemic exacerbated economic difficulties but also provided Bukele opportunity to concentrate power.

events.title: Congress Conflict Incident
events.description: President Bukele led military and police into Legislative Assembly, attempting to force congress to approve international loan for security plan. Bukele summoned supporters to rally outside congress, with armed soldiers occupying assembly hall, Bukele praying in presidential seat, creating dramatic scene. Many congress members were absent, boycotting presidential pressure. Incident triggered constitutional crisis, with opposition condemning as coup attempt, international community including United States and EU expressing concern. Bukele supporters claimed he defended people against corrupt politicians. Incident showed Bukele's confrontational governing style and disrespect for democratic institutions. Bukele used social media to defend actions, claiming legislators obstructed security efforts. Incident intensified political polarization, raising concerns about El Salvador's democratic stability. Despite controversy, Bukele's popularity remained high, showing popular desire for strongman leadership.

events.title: Nuevas Ideas Party Congressional Majority
events.description: Bukele's Nuevas Ideas party won overwhelming victory in congressional elections, gaining 56 of 84 seats, achieving absolute majority. Victory enabled Bukele to control legislative agenda without needing opposition compromise. Election results reflected Bukele's high popularity and rejection of traditional parties ARENA and FMLN, both parties' seats sharply reduced. After gaining congressional control, Bukele government quickly acted to reshape state institutions. May 1, new congress dismissed five Supreme Court justices and Attorney General, replacing with Bukele allies. Action triggered domestic and international condemnation, viewed as attack on judicial independence and democratic backsliding. United States and EU criticized and threatened sanctions. Bukele defended as cleaning corrupt institutions, gaining popular support. Institutional reorganization gave Bukele nearly complete control over three government branches, raising warnings about authoritarianism. However, Bukele insisted on serving people's will, opposing elite corruption.

events.title: Bitcoin Becomes Legal Tender
events.description: El Salvador became world's first country to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender, Bukele's signature initiative. Government launched Chivo digital wallet, providing each citizen $30 in Bitcoin to encourage use. Bukele claimed Bitcoin would promote financial inclusion, lower remittance costs, and attract investment. Government purchased hundreds of Bitcoins, planning to build 'Bitcoin City' and use volcanic geothermal for mining. However, plan was highly controversial, with economists and international institutions like IMF warning of risks, including price volatility, money laundering, and fiscal instability. Polls showed most Salvadorans didn't understand or trust Bitcoin. Chivo wallet launch encountered technical problems, usage rate lower than expected. Opposition criticized as gimmick, diverting attention from real problems. Bitcoin price volatility led to government losses of tens of millions of dollars. However, Bukele persisted with Bitcoin strategy, self-promoting on international stage as cryptocurrency pioneer.

events.title: State of Emergency and Anti-Gang Offensive
events.description: After gang violence surge led to 87 deaths in three days, Bukele government declared state of emergency, suspending constitutional rights. Congress approved 'exception regime,' allowing detention without evidence, extending pretrial detention, limiting assembly and communication privacy. Government launched massive anti-gang offensive, arresting over 60,000 suspected gang members within months. Police and military conducted large-scale sweeps, surrounding communities, searching house by house. New prison 'Terrorism Confinement Center' (CECOT) built, Americas' largest prison, capable of holding 40,000 prisoners. Prison conditions extremely harsh, with prisoners in solitary confinement 23 hours daily, minimum food, no visits or sunlight. Offensive significantly lowered murder rate, from over 10 daily to less than 2 daily. Bukele's popularity soared above 90%, with people celebrating security improvements. However, human rights organizations documented thousands of arbitrary detention, torture, and prison death cases. Many arrested were not gang members, detained based on appearance or residence. International community criticized human rights violations, but Bukele ignored criticism, claiming protecting people was priority.

events.title: Announcement of Reelection Campaign
events.description: Bukele formally announced reelection campaign, despite Salvadoran constitution prohibiting consecutive reelection. Bukele-appointed Supreme Court ruled constitutional prohibition didn't apply to his case, allowing him to run. Decision triggered constitutional crisis and international criticism, viewed as manipulating law to maintain power. Opposition and constitutional scholars condemned as unconstitutional, but lacked power to prevent. Bukele's reelection campaign based on anti-gang offensive success and promise to restore security. Polls showed he had overwhelming support, over 80%. Opposition was divided and weakened, unable to provide credible alternative. Bukele's campaign slogan 'The Next Chapter of History,' promoting continuity of security and economic development. Critics warned El Salvador was heading toward one-party authoritarianism, with democratic institutions being hollowed out. International community, particularly United States, expressed concern but had limited influence. Bukele used populist narrative, portraying opposition as elites and foreign interference, defending people's will.

events.title: Contemporary El Salvador: Achievements and Challenges
events.description: 2024 El Salvador is a contradictory country. Security significantly improved, murder rate dropped to historic low, people can move freely, businesses flourish, tourism recovers. Bukele government promotes infrastructure projects, including libraries, schools, and parks, improving urban appearance. International investment increases, economy shows recovery signs. However, security achievements built on mass incarceration and human rights violations, with over 70,000 detained, most without due process. Democratic institutions weakened, judiciary, legislature, and media controlled by executive. Freedom of expression restricted, journalists and critics face threats. Corruption allegations plague government, transparency lacking. Economy though improved, poverty and inequality persist, with about 30% population living below poverty line. Climate change exacerbates drought and food insecurity. Migration though reduced continues, seeking better opportunities. Bitcoin experiment failed to deliver promises, fiscal sustainability questioned. El Salvador struggles between security and freedom, order and democracy. Bukele's legacy will depend on whether security improvements can build inclusive and sustainable future, or merely establish another Latin American authoritarian regime. Salvadoran people, having experienced colonialism, dictatorship, civil war, and now populist authoritarianism, continue seeking peace, prosperity, and dignity.

events.title: Bukele Reelection Victory
events.description: Bukele won reelection in presidential election with overwhelming over 80% vote rate, with Nuevas Ideas party gaining 54 of 60 congressional seats, achieving supermajority. Victory reflected popular satisfaction with security improvements and support for Bukele's personal charisma. Opposition candidates received only single-digit percentages. Voter turnout about 52%, lower than expected. Despite constitutional controversy, people endorsed Bukele with votes. International observers raised concerns about election process, including media inequality, opposition marginalization, and legal ambiguity. However, domestic celebrations, with Bukele supporters viewing as historic victory. Victory consolidated Bukele's dominance over Salvadoran politics, with almost no checks and balances. Bukele promised to continue security offensive, promote economic development and infrastructure construction. Critics worried about further democratic erosion, authoritarianism consolidation. However, for many Salvadorans, ability to walk streets without fear was more important than democratic norms.
